ab: X. Let us learn to do: (Jumping Jack frog – paper plate craft)
Things needed: 1. paper plate 2. green and black paint 3. brush 4. scissors 5. red felt paper 6. green and white chart paper 7. glue
Paper plate, green and black paint, brush, scissors, red felt paper, green and white chart paper, glue.
Steps to make the frog (Step 1 to Step 4)

ಹಂತ 1: Paint the paper plate green. When it is thoroughly dry, fold the plate in half.
ಹಂತ 2: Cut a 3 x 7 inch 'tongue' from the red felt paper and stick it on the centre of the fold.
ಹಂತ 3: For the eyes, cut a pair of 1 x 2 inch white rectangles and round the upper edges. Fold each in half and glue the lower portion to the top of the plate. Add black eyeballs with black paint.
ಹಂತ 4: Cut frog legs out of green chart paper: a shorter set for the front and a long, bent pair for the back.

ab: 1. How was Nithin's tricycle to look at?
It was a cute little tricycle with three wheels and a horn that went 'Pom! Pom! Pom!'; it also had pedals and a beautiful seat.
2. Why was the tricycle angry with Nithin?
Because Nithin would not let it go to the main road to race with cars and buses; he said he would ride only in the compound.
3. What did the tricycle do when Nithin was away at the playschool?
It rolled out of the compound, into a narrow lane, and then onto the main road full of cars, buses and lorries.
4. What lesson did the tricycle learn that day?
It learnt that it should never roll out of the compound again, and that Nithin was right.

A fairy whose head had the shape of a tooth.

Because the small tooth fitted his mouth just right; it was not sharp, did not stick out and was not too big.

ab: 1. Why did the fawn feel frustrated?
Because his mother did not allow him to go alone to places, though he was grown up.
2. What did the fawn do when its mother was asleep?
He slipped out alone, went to an open field to play, and then went to a stream to drink water.
3. What answer did the fawn give to the lion?
'Sir, how can I spoil the water? It is flowing from your side towards me.'
What is the moral of the story?
Children should obey their parents in order to avoid getting into difficulties.
